coordinates.heading: compass direction the front door faces: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west

landmarks.name: Great Tower (the Keep)
landmarks.desc: 28 m stone keep, last refuge of the castle; four storeys.

landmarks.name: Inner Ward & Great Hall
landmarks.desc: Lord's hall, chapel and kitchens behind a second wall.

landmarks.name: Great Gatehouse
landmarks.desc: Twin drum towers, portcullis and murder holes.

landmarks.name: Drawbridge & Barbican
landmarks.desc: Lifting bridge over the moat, guarded by a walled barbican.

landmarks.name: Castle Moat
landmarks.desc: Spring-fed moat ringing the castle plateau.

landmarks.name: Postern Gate
landmarks.desc: Small north door to the ridge paths and watch posts.

landmarks.name: Market Square
landmarks.desc: Heart of the town: market hall, cross, well and stalls.

landmarks.name: St. Michael's Church
landmarks.desc: Parish church with a 36 m spire, the tallest thing in the vale.

landmarks.name: Guildhall
landmarks.desc: Where the merchant guild meets and the town court sits.

landmarks.name: The Ford & Crown
landmarks.desc: The town's great inn - travellers, gossip and quests.

landmarks.name: Steward's Hall - YOUR HOUSE
landmarks.desc: Home of The Steward. Start your journey here.

landmarks.name: Town gates (N, W, E & River Gate)
landmarks.desc: Four gatehouses close at curfew.

landmarks.name: St. Hilda's Abbey
landmarks.desc: Benedictine abbey: church, cloister, infirmary and pilgrims' house.

landmarks.name: Abbey fishponds
landmarks.desc: Three stew ponds that feed the monks on fast days.

landmarks.name: Westbrook green & chapel
landmarks.desc: Village green, pond, maypole and chapel.

landmarks.name: Eastmere & Eastmere Water
landmarks.desc: Fishing village on a reed-fringed mere.

landmarks.name: Southfold
landmarks.desc: Shepherds' hamlet with a great stone sheep pen.

landmarks.name: Raven Hill Watchtower
landmarks.desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

landmarks.name: Beacon Hill Watchtower
landmarks.desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

landmarks.name: West Tor Watchtower
landmarks.desc: Lookout with a signal beacon, in sight of the castle keep.

landmarks.name: Greycrown Beacon
landmarks.desc: Highest point of the vale: the great warning fire.

landmarks.name: The Nine Maidens
landmarks.desc: Ancient ring of nine stones older than the castle. Locals leave offerings.

landmarks.name: The Old Ash Ford
landmarks.desc: Shallow crossing where the first settlers forded the Ash - the vale's namesake.

landmarks.name: Ashford Watermill
landmarks.desc: Grinds the vale's grain; the miller takes one sack in sixteen.

landmarks.name: Tannery
landmarks.desc: Smelly work kept downstream and outside the walls.

landmarks.name: Post Windmill
landmarks.desc: Turns to face the wind on a single great post.

landmarks.name: Tiltyard
landmarks.desc: Jousting lists for the summer tourney.

landmarks.name: Quarry
landmarks.desc: Where the castle's stone was cut. Still worked today.

landmarks.name: King's Chase Lodge
landmarks.desc: Royal hunting lodge deep in the deer forest.

landmarks.name: Charcoal Burners' Camp
landmarks.desc: Smoke rises day and night from the Wildwood clearing.

landmarks.name: Ash Bridge
landmarks.desc: Three-arched stone bridge below the River Gate.

landmarks.name: East Bridge
landmarks.desc: Timber bridge carrying the King's Road east.
